turkisha1.subtitle: {notes} words · both directions, as two cards per word
descSub: The cards are ordered by that frequency, so the words met most often come first; the 10 two-word expressions, which a list of single words cannot count, come last.

The list was drawn by that frequency, and after the first 100 cards the order still follows it (the end of this description says how); the two-word expressions the list itself held, which a list of single words cannot count, come last, but for hafta sonu, which stands with the days.
turkisha1.tail: THE BEGINNER PASS (Nov 2026). The figures above describe the list as the frequency dealt it. The deck is now {notes} notes, {cards} cards: those 500, and {added} a beginner needs that the list did not hold. Sixteen everyday formulas that were cards of the phrases deck, the last on the shelf (teşekkür ederim, rica ederim, iyi günler, iyi akşamlar, iyi geceler, hoşça kal, güle güle, adınız ne, benim adım, memnun oldum, kolay gelsin, afiyet olsun, geçmiş olsun and three more); selam, günaydın, affedersiniz, pardon, ad, su and içmek, which were cards of A2; sağ ol and buyurun, of B1; hoş geldiniz, sıfır, the fourth and fifth ordinals and two colours (kahverengi, gri), of B2. And seven that no deck held, each built from its English Wiktionary entry as every other card is: the question particle mi and the word de ("too"), written apart, which the frequency list could not tell from suffixes; nasılsın, nasılsınız and görüşürüz, one-word formulas; ne kadar; and özür dilemek, whose sentences are the apology özür dilerim. THE ORDER is a teaching order first and frequency after: the first 100 notes are written by hand — the greetings and courtesies, the pronouns, a first exchange, this and that, var, yok and değil with mi and de, ten verbs, the question words, zero to ten, and five formulas for a guest, a worker, a meal and the sick — and the rest follow by frequency with each closed set together: twenty to a thousand and the ordinals from note 121, the days from note 151, the months and the seasons from note 161, the colours from note 201, the compass points from note 301. THE PACE: the app gives ten new cards a day, both directions together, which is five words a day: merhaba and teşekkür ederim on day one, good morning to good night on day {day:günaydın}, nasılsın on day {day:nasılsın}, the first verbs on day {day:olmak}, the question words from day {day:nerede}, zero to ten on days {day:sıfır} and {day:on}; {days} days for the deck. Taken in the shelf's order — the sounds deck, A1, A2, B1, B2, C1, the phrases — A1 runs from day {from} to day {to}, B1 is reached on day {turkishb1.from}, and the whole shelf is {shelfNotes} notes, {shelfDays} days, {shelfYears} years. The sounds deck (Turkish — Sounds and spelling: how the letters are read, where the stress falls and how the suffixes on these cards change with the word) can be studied beside A1 instead of before it. WHAT A CARD SHOWS SINCE THIS PASS: a noun's row ends with two possessed forms, "my" and "his, her" (kitabım, kitabı; arabam, arabası) — a fifth of the words in these sentences were suffixed forms of an A1 word that no card showed, and the possessed forms were the largest part; a verb's row adds the negative of the present and the two commands, to sen and to siz (gitmiyor; git, gidin); o and bu show their plurals (onlar, bunlar), which are no cards of their own; and a sentence is no longer matched to a word by a form that is another word's spelling (on, "ten", by onu, "him"; demek by de, "too"). SEN AND SIZ: sen is one person you know well; siz is several people, or one person addressed politely. A formula made for siz is its polite form (nasılsınız, adınız ne, affedersiniz, hoş geldiniz, buyurun), and the command shown for siz is the one to use with a stranger. NOT HERE, because the English Wiktionary has no entry of its own to build the card from: nereye ("where to") and onlar ("they"; it is on o's row), which it files only as forms of another word, ne zaman ("when"), özür dilerim and iyiyim ("I am fine"; the phrases deck has iyiyim, teşekkürler) as cards of one word, and the names Türkçe and Türkiye.

trphrase.subtitle: {notes} expressions · {phrases} everyday, {idioms} idioms, {proverbs} proverbs · both directions
descSub: Within each subdeck the expressions are ordered by how often they occur in Tatoeba's Turkish sentences, an expression ending in a verb being counted in any form of that verb, so the ones met most often come first.

Within each subdeck the expressions come by reading level (the end of this description says how), and inside a level by how often they occurred in Tatoeba's Turkish sentences when the deck was first built, an expression ending in a verb being counted in any form of that verb.
trphrase.tail: THE BEGINNER PASS (Nov 2026). The figures above describe the list as it was drawn. The deck is now {notes} expressions — {phrases} everyday phrases, {idioms} idioms and {proverbs} proverbs — because {left} everyday formulas (teşekkür ederim, rica ederim, bir şey değil, iyi günler, iyi akşamlar, iyi geceler, hoşça kal, güle güle, benim adım, adınız ne, memnun oldum, hoş bulduk, kolay gelsin, afiyet olsun, geçmiş olsun, saat kaç) are now cards of Turkish A1, where a beginner meets them in the first weeks and not after C1; a reader who already holds them here keeps them. THE ORDER inside each subdeck is by reading level: first the expressions every word of which is on a card of Turkish A1, a suffixed form counting only if a card shows it, then A2, B1, B2 and C1, and last those that use a word or a form no level shows — which is most of them, since an idiom is a sentence in miniature and its words are inflected. So this deck can be begun beside A1 and need not wait for C1; the idioms and proverbs are for a reader who has the levels behind them. THE PACE: the app gives ten new cards a day, both directions together, which is five expressions a day, {days} days for this deck; taken last in the shelf's order it runs from day {from} to day {to}.
